name: Michel Fournier
party: Sans étiquette (no party affiliation; generally described as divers droite, occasionally classed on the left)
bio: Michel Fournier, born 11 January 1950 in Châtel-sur-Moselle (Vosges), is a French local politician and a leading public figure for rural France (la ruralité). Born into a family of farmers from Bouxières-aux-Bois, he left school without a diploma, worked early jobs as an agricultural labourer and shutter fitter, spent time in Germany at 17, passed the customs service exam in 1968, and did his military service at Yutz in 1969. He settled in Les Voivres in 1972 and worked as a multi-line commercial agent. He entered the municipal council of Les Voivres in 1983 and has been the village's mayor since 1989. He founded and led the Association des maires ruraux des Vosges from 1992, served as secretary-general then first vice-president of the Association des maires ruraux de France (AMRF), and was elected president of the AMRF in November 2020, succeeding Vanik Berberian (presidency held 2020-2025). He has also been vice-president of the Communauté d'agglomération d'Épinal (since 2017, in charge of territorial cohesion and rurality) and vice-president of the Agence nationale de la cohésion des territoires (ANCT, 2021-2025). On 12 October 2025 he was appointed Minister-Delegate for Rurality in the second government of Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, a post he retained after the 26 February 2026 reshuffle. He sits without party affiliation (sans étiquette). He is married and the father of three children, and was made a Chevalier of the Légion d'honneur (decree of 31 December 2021).
